The FTRL-type algorithm has been demonstrated to achieve BoTW results for many problems including MAB (Zimmert and Seldin, 2019; Ito, 2021b), combinatorial MAB (Zimmert et al., 2019; Ito, 2021a), graph feedback (Erez and Koren, 2021; Ito et al., 2022), and MDP (Jin and Luo, 2020; Jin et al., 2021). However, the question of whether this algorithm can achieve BoTW results for the canonical linear bandit problem remains open. To the best of our knowledge, Theorem 1 provides the first BoTW results for linear bandits with FTRL algorithm. Although our results have not reached the optimal order in separate settings (Lattimore and Szepesvari, 2017; Bubeck et al., 2012), the convergence result itself is significant because it not only provides a more concise algorithm for this problem with only detect-switch-based methods available previously but also discovers the potential of FTRL-type algorithms.
